content:
{'index': 0, 'text': 'The 28-year-old female model and daughter-in-law of Tam\'s Noodle founder, Tsai Tien-feng (Abby Choi), was murdered and dismembered in 2023. Her ex-husband Kwong Kong-chi, former father-in-law Kwong Kau, and former brother-in-law Kwong Kong-kit have been charged with murder and preventing the lawful burial of a body. Tsai Tien-feng\'s mother, Cheung Yin-fa, continued to give evidence today (the 6th), mentioning that when Tsai Tien-feng wanted to sell the Kowloon Tong residence registered under Kwong Kau\'s name, the two sides had multiple disputes, during which Kwong Kau told the mother and daughter "If you dare (sell it), I\'ll kill your whole family," and that Tsai Tien-feng had said Kwong Kau had hit her. Audio recordings of Tsai Tien-feng with her mother were played in court, in which Tsai Tien-feng described Kwong Kau as an "old thief" and criticised the Kwong family for "having such a life and not even being grateful." The prosecution then played footage of a property viewing at the Kowloon Tong house taken on the day of the incident before Tsai Tien-feng was killed. Tsai\'s mother wailed, saying "I don\'t want to watch," adding "I really regret it, my daughter was so good," and that the Kwong family "really bit the hand that feeds them." The court adjourned and will continue hearing the case in the afternoon. Related report: Abby Choi case | Mother gives evidence, repeatedly says the Kwong family had "no money," describes the relationship as friendly and "obliging" — Kwong Kau smirks upon hearing this'}

{'index': 1, 'text': "Tsai Tien-feng's mother Cheung Yin-fa is giving evidence for a second day today. Tsai Tien-feng's father continues to attend the hearing. (File photo)"}

{'index': 2, 'text': 'Hainan property, Shenzhen Rolls-Royce and others registered under Kwong Kau — Tsai Tien-feng wanted to take them back'}

{'index': 3, 'text': 'The case continued at the High Court today, with Tsai Tien-feng\'s father again attending the hearing. Cheung Yin-fa testified that from June 2022, Tsai Tien-feng planned to sell the Kowloon Tong unit registered under Kwong Kau\'s name and asked Kwong Kau to sign a power of attorney, but Kwong Kau refused. Cheung had also called to try to persuade him. Cheung said Kwong Kau stated on the phone that "this flat is not for sale," describing his attitude as "very vicious" and threatening "If you dare, I\'ll kill your whole family." Kwong Kau, in the dock, frowned and smirked upon hearing this. Cheung also said Tsai Tien-feng had told her "If you want to buy a flat, I\'ll kill you," and that Kwong Kau had hit her.'}

{'index': 4, 'text': 'The court played several WeChat voice messages between Tsai Tien-feng and Cheung Yin-fa, in which Tsai mentioned to her mother that she had "given him the car, watches, etc. in the mainland." Cheung explained this referred to properties purchased by her daughter in Hainan but registered under Kwong Kau\'s name; after the dispute with the Kwong family, "my daughter wanted to take back everything." Kwong Kau was initially unwilling to sell, and only signed the power of attorney after she threatened to take him to court. Tsai\'s mother further said Kwong Kau had two cars registered under his name, including a Rolls-Royce in Shenzhen and a black seven-seater, because Kwong Kong-chi "said he needed them for business." During this, the judge Mr Justice Kei Yan-fai asked why the cars were registered under Kwong Kau rather than Kwong Kong-chi. Tsai\'s mother said Kwong Kong-chi had specified they be registered under his father\'s name, "saying to use his father\'s name because he could not use his own."'}

{'index': 5, 'text': 'Tsai Tien-feng called Kwong Kau an "old thief" — criticised the Kwong family for being ungrateful'}

{'index': 6, 'text': 'In the recording, Tsai\'s mother told Tsai Tien-feng that "these people bite the hand that feeds them." Under examination-in-chief, she said she felt disappointed with the Kwong family, and mentioned that she had advised her daughter that "what she should take back, she should take back." She said she had initially supported helping the Kwong family, but disputes arose when it came to selling the flat and mainland assets, with talk of "killing and hacking." She said Tsai Tien-feng stated she would slowly sort out the watches under Kwong Kong-chi\'s name, the two cars under Kwong Kau\'s name, and the Hainan property. In a recording, Tsai Tien-feng described Kwong Kau to her mother as an "old thief," saying "I raised his son, raised him and his wife," and in another recording criticised the Kwong family for not knowing gratitude: "Having such a life and not even knowing to thank me."'}

{'index': 7, 'text': 'Tsai\'s mother also testified that Li Sui-heung and her husband often spoke ill of Tsai Tien-feng in front of her children, telling the grandchildren "don\'t listen to Mummy," which was a source of conflict between the two sides. In a recording played in court, Tsai\'s mother asked "What did Grandma teach you?" A child\'s voice replied, "Grandma said Mummy is crazy." Tsai\'s mother then asked, "And what did I (i.e. she) teach you to say?" The child replied, "We must love each other and must not argue."'}

{'index': 8, 'text': "Court plays footage taken before Tsai Tien-feng was killed — Tsai's mother wails"}

{'index': 9, 'text': 'In another recording, Tsai Tien-feng was in France and told her mother that the Kwong family was preventing her from seeing the children during Lunar New Year, not allowing her to contact or talk to them. Tsai Tien-feng said in the recording to her mother: "Call his mother, his mother says she doesn\'t know, says maybe he\'s with Alex; call his brother, his brother says he\'s driving… call Alex and he says he doesn\'t know," and "Call brother, and they say maybe he\'s with his dad." Tsai\'s mother said after Tsai returned to Hong Kong she visited the children at home every day, and after Kwong Kau signed the power of attorney at the end of 2022, she no longer allowed Kwong Kau to come to the house. In another recording, Tsai Tien-feng told her mother that her lawyer advised her to sell the flat quickly, because if anything happened to Kwong Kau, his wife would have the right to inherit the unit. Tsai also mentioned that the power of attorney from Kwong Kau could be revoked at any time, saying she had listed the flat with five or six estate agents, saying "Losing a few million is better than having the house cheated away," and asked her mother to make inquiries. In February 2023, a friend of Tsai\'s mother, "Sister Ling," said "a mainland immigrant" wanted to buy the Kowloon Tong luxury property.'}

{'index': 10, 'text': 'The prosecution played closed-circuit television footage from inside the Kowloon Tong house at 1:12 pm on 21 February 2023, the day Tsai Tien-feng was killed. The footage showed Tsai Tien-feng in the house greeting visitors at the main door and introducing the unit, saying "There are six floors in total here," among other things. Less than half a minute into the footage, Tsai\'s mother cried out, "I don\'t want to watch," adding, "I really regret it. My daughter was so good, she was so filial, really, she was kind to the wrong people." During this, Kwong Kau and Kwong Kong-chi frowned, while Kwong Kong-kit rubbed his nose. The lead prosecutor said no more footage of Tsai Tien-feng would be played. Tsai\'s mother said, "They really did bite the hand that feeds them," while Tsai\'s father in the public gallery had tears in his eyes.'}

{'index': 11, 'text': 'The judge ordered a short adjournment, with the hearing to resume in the afternoon.'}
